cases.meaning: Given the declared complete formula, the correct observation matches; this is not a new business run.
The same independently supplied formula contradicts the actual Cycle3 amount; original scoring stays untouched.
A required input is unavailable, so the prototype cannot convert the gap to a numeric zero or a match.
The supplied formula contradicts a hypothetical earlier observation. This control supplies no historical fee or dependency invalidation implementation.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: a wrong but legal method still matches a wrong business value. A schema/calculator does not prove method validity or independence.
STRONGER COUNTEREXAMPLE: the author omits relevant inputs as well as the method. The comparison cannot recover facts outside its declared record.
Literal comparison can represent non-numeric effects when their expected ordered record is supplied independently.
A supplied expectation of three effects exposes a Slack-only observation as incomplete; this is an operator-authored control.
An unavailable observation remains unresolved even with a complete formula.
Different declared units yield an explicit unresolved contract relationship, not implicit conversion.
A declared divide-by-zero method yields an explicit domain error; it is never a business verdict.
A non-terminating decimal method with no rounding policy yields an explicit precision limit instead of a silently rounded comparison.
A nonnumeric string maps to an exact schema error path rather than being silently coerced.
